$comment: Every repository here was read by a human, and every expected finding below was
checked against the source and judged correct-as-stated. Commits are PINNED so a
drift in this corpus means OUR behaviour changed, never that upstream did.
`expected` lists finding codes with their occurrence count. `notes` records WHY a
finding is expected — several are known false positives kept deliberately, so that
when one is fixed the harness fails and forces this file to be updated rather than

repos.name: node-express-boilerplate
repos.why: Express + Mongoose + Passport monolith with compose override files. Exercises compose-override unification and Maven-free manifest naming.

notes.IR-LINT-DIRECT-DB-ACCESS-002: Known limitation, kept: the app is one gateway node, so this reports 'no service layer visible' rather than asserting a defect. The repo IS layered (controllers -> services -> models).
notes.IR-LINT-NO-HEALTHCHECK-003: TRUE. src/routes/v1 has auth, user and docs routes only; no health endpoint anywhere.

repos.name: lokalise-node-service-template
repos.why: Fastify + drizzle + @fastify/jwt. Regression guard for object-form route detection and scoped auth-plugin detection.

notes.IR-LINT-DIRECT-DB-ACCESS-002: Manifest-only edge, so it arrives low-confidence and hedged.
notes.IR-LINT-ISOLATED-NODE-005: fauxqs, a local SQS/SNS emulator, genuinely has no depends_on. Factually true, low value.
notes.absent-NO-HEALTHCHECK: Must NOT fire: /live is declared via app.route({ url }) and is detected since the Fastify object-form fix.
notes.absent-MISSING-AUTH: Must NOT fire: @fastify/jwt is detected as an auth node.

repos.name: spring-petclinic
repos.why: Java: pom.xml + compose + k8s, no code analyser. Guards Maven parent-POM naming, whose fix also unifies the manifest and Kubernetes views by canonical id.

notes.clean: Zero findings. The component must be named 'petclinic' from <name>, never 'spring-boot-starter-parent' from the inherited <parent> block.

repos.name: example-voting-app
repos.why: Polyglot monorepo, compose + k8s, several services built from subdirectories. Guards against over-eager scan-root merging.

notes.sut-must-stay-separate: The `sut` test harness builds from ./tests/ and must NOT fold into the app root. An earlier build-context heuristic wrongly merged it.
notes.IR-LINT-MISSING-AUTH-010: Known limitation: fires on the whole-app node, which carries the same weakness DIRECT-DB-ACCESS shed.

repos.name: full-stack-fastapi-template
repos.why: Python + compose with an override that re-declares `db` without an image. Direct regression guard for the type-specificity bug that relabelled Postgres as a gateway.

notes.db-must-be-postgres: compose.yml declares `db: image: postgres:18`; compose.override.yml re-declares `db` with only ports. The identified postgres type must win over the guessed gateway.
notes.known-noise: adminer / proxy / traefik are dev tooling promoted to gateways on published ports; the MISSING-AUTH and ISOLATED-NODE counts reflect that unresolved limitation.

repos.name: eShopOnWeb
repos.why: .NET + compose. Only corpus entry exercising the C# analyser path.

notes.known-noise: An [Authorize] auth node IS detected but is not connected to the compose-derived gateways, so MISSING-AUTH fires anyway. Fixing that linkage should drop these to 0 and update this entry.

repos.name: microservices-demo
repos.why: Kubernetes-native polyglot. Tracks the *_SERVICE_ADDR extraction gap — the largest known scan-quality deficit.

notes.resolved-2026-08: Was 12 isolated nodes, caused by the Kubernetes extractor ignoring *_SERVICE_ADDR wiring. With those edges extracted the graph is the real Online Boutique topology (21 edges), and the counts below were re-adjudicated against it.
notes.IR-LINT-ISOLATED-NODE-005: TRUE, both of them. opentelemetrycollector is referenced by no env address anywhere in the manifests, and the terraform state bucket is genuinely standalone infrastructure.
notes.IR-LINT-HIGH-FANOUT-004: TRUE. frontend calls 8 services and checkoutservice calls 6; that is the actual shape of this application and worth surfacing.
notes.IR-LINT-SYNC-CHAIN-001: TRUE. ingress → frontend → checkoutservice → leaf is a real 4-hop synchronous chain.
notes.IR-LINT-DEAD-NODE-011: Rose from 2 to 6 because the graph is now connected: adservice, emailservice, paymentservice and currencyservice are leaf gRPC services that legitimately terminate. Same known weakness as auth nodes — the rule fires on anything that receives without emitting. Not a regression from this change.

repos.name: petclinic-micro
repos.why: Multi-module Maven + compose, wired through Spring Cloud Config and Eureka. The corpus entry for the service-discovery gap, and the guard for naming a component from an artifact-repository <name>.

notes.REPOSITORY-NAME-FIXED: Why this repo was added. spring-petclinic-genai-service/pom.xml declares no project <name>, and its <repositories> block at :148 does — so 'Spring Milestones', a Maven artifact repository, became a component AND drew a driver edge to mysql. A node by that name here means the fix regressed. Same class as the <parent> bug: the name must come from the project's own header.
notes.IR-LINT-ISOLATED-NODE-005: 3, all TRUE as stated. grafana-server and prometheus-server build from ./docker/* and have no depends_on; tracing-server (zipkin) likewise. Services really do report to zipkin, but only via config served by config-server at runtime — nothing in the compose file declares it, so the honest answer is that we cannot see it.
notes.service-discovery: The documented gap, visible here in its mildest form. depends_on gives us every service -> config-server / discovery-server edge, so the graph is connected — but the service-to-service calls that Eureka resolves at runtime (api-gateway -> customers/vets/visits) are absent, and nothing in the manifests could tell us about them. The 9 MULTIPLE-HTTP-ENTRIES are that absence showing through.
notes.IR-LINT-MISSING-AUTH-010: 9, the whole-app-node weakness. Every compose service is one node standing in for a Spring Boot application, so the rule asserts against components whose auth we cannot see.
notes.IR-LINT-NO-HEALTHCHECK-003: TRUE as stated, low value. The compose healthchecks probe `/` (docker-compose.yml:10, :25), not a health path, and Spring Boot's /actuator/health lives in Java code we have no analyser for.
notes.cross-tier: Compose `customers-service` and Maven `spring-petclinic-customers-service` stay separate nodes. Adjudicated as acceptable rather than correct: the two tiers genuinely disagree on the name, and guessing they are the same component is exactly the kind of inference this scanner is supposed to refuse. It is why the node count is 16 rather than ~12.

repos.name: podinfo
repos.why: Go + Kubernetes + compose + a committed OpenAPI spec. The corpus entry that exercises CONTAINER-ARG wiring, and the first to exercise CronJob workloads and the OpenAPI API-node fan-out.

notes.ARGS-WIRING-FIXED: Why this repo was added, and now its regression guard. podinfo wires every service through container `command:`/`args:`, never env: deploy/bases/frontend/deployment.yaml:44 `--backend-url=http://backend:9898/echo` and :45 `--cache-server=tcp://cache:6379`, deploy/bases/backend/deployment.yaml:45, repeated in deploy/webapp/frontend/deployment.yaml:45 and deploy/secure/. The Kubernetes extractor read only `env`, so all of it was invisible and ISOLATED-NODE stood at 14. Reading args closed it: frontend->backend, frontend->cache and backend->cache are now extracted, and the count is 12. If it climbs back to 14 the arg rule has regressed.
notes.IR-LINT-ISOLATED-NODE-005: 9, of which 5 are TRUE. TRUE: database-primary and database-replica (nothing anywhere in the repo declares a connection to either — they are a demo topology with no client), and backup-daily / rollup-daily / rollup-weekly (their containers run a mounted shell script and carry only scalar env like BACKUP_EXIT=1, so there is genuinely no address to read). The remaining 4 are known gaps, by cause: (a) warm-cache carries FRONTEND_URL=http://frontend at deploy/bases/frontend/cronjob-warm-cache.yaml:33 — `_URL` is deliberately excluded from ADDRESS_SHAPED_KEY and the value has no explicit port, so it fails both halves of the test; (b) grafana, loki and jaeger are really connected — otel/grafana-datasources.yaml:6 and :10 point Grafana at both — but that is a Grafana provisioning file mounted as a volume, not a topology manifest, and is legitimately out of scope.
notes.COMPOSE-WIRING-FIXED: Was 12. otel/docker-compose.yaml declares its wiring the two ways the compose tier could not read: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://otel:4317 at :8 and :15 (an arbitrary env key, AND a URL value that composePlainEnvHostname rejects outright), and `--backend-url http://podinfo_backend:9899/status/200` at :6 (a command flag). All three edges now extract — podinfo_frontend->otel, podinfo_backend->otel, podinfo_frontend->podinfo_backend — clearing gateway_otel and gateway_podinfo_backend. podinfo_frontend stays an HTTP entry, correctly: it is the published entrypoint and nothing calls it.
notes.IR-LINT-HIGH-FANOUT-004: Known limitation, kept deliberately. Fires on gateway_podinfo_api with 26 outgoing edges, which is simply the 26 operations of pkg/api/http/docs/swagger.yaml hanging off the API node the openapi tier creates to front them. That is spec size, not architectural fan-out. First corpus repo to trip this, and the reason it is worth pinning.
notes.IR-LINT-MISSING-AUTH-010: 5, all technically true, most low value. swagger.yaml declares no securityDefinitions and no per-operation `security:` block, so podinfo-api is unauthenticated as specified — though /token and /token/validate (swagger.yaml:419, :434) mint and check JWTs, an auth capability we do not model as an auth node. grafana is the one worth saying out loud: otel/docker-compose.yaml:35 sets GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_ENABLED=true with ORG_ROLE=Admin. jaeger and loki are an unauthenticated local observability stack — factually true, not advice. Was 7: otel and podinfo_backend dropped off once they had incoming edges and stopped counting as entry nodes.
notes.IR-LINT-MULTIPLE-HTTP-ENTRIES-009: One finding, now naming 5 nodes rather than 7 — grafana, jaeger, loki, podinfo_api and podinfo_frontend. Partly downstream of the remaining gaps rather than independently meaningful, though podinfo_frontend genuinely is the entrypoint.
notes.cross-tier: gateway_podinfo_api (from the spec title 'Podinfo API') stays separate from service_podinfo (the kustomize/ Deployment). Correct as adjudicated — nothing in either file declares that this workload serves that spec, so unifying them would be a guess.

repos.name: terraform-aws-eks
repos.why: Pure HCL. The only corpus entry exercising the Terraform tier, and a direct guard for the placeholder-label naming fix.

notes.clean: Zero findings, and that is the correct answer: a Terraform module declares infrastructure, not a running system, so there is no topology to lint.
notes.naming: The SQS queue is declared as `resource "aws_sqs_queue" "this"`. It must be named `sqs queue` from the resource type — a node called `this` means the placeholder-label fallback regressed.
notes.KNOWN-THIN: 2 nodes from 185 files. The tier reads resources it recognises and ignores the rest, so this is a depth limit rather than a correctness one. A larger node count here is an improvement, not a regression — re-adjudicate rather than assume.
